scenes.title: True, but wrong
scenes.text: This citation is real. This sentence has nothing to do with it. Yet for provenance, everything checks out: the quote exists, it is identical to the document, the token is valid. Nobody asked the one question that matters: does this quote actually support this sentence?

scenes.title: Provenance is not meaning
scenes.text: A verified citation can still be a wrong citation. The provenance check only asks whether the words exist in the document. It never checks meaning. So an agent can take a real quote and staple it to a fact about something else.

scenes.title: One question, three answers
scenes.text: The new question is a single one: does the evidence support the claim? Three answers: supported, unrelated, contradicted. One pass, no generation. A line passes only if at least one quote supports it and none contradicts it. A contradiction always wins. If the check fails, the answer is not published, and the model tries again.

scenes.title: 150 pairs, two numbers
scenes.text: To prove it, we built a test set: a hundred and fifty claim-quote pairs, labelled by hand, sixty in Italian, sixty in dev, thirty held out for test. Two numbers matter: false accepts, wrong citations let through; and false rejects, correct citations blocked. The target: cut false accepts by sixty percent, and keep false rejects under ten.

scenes.title: The local model is not enough
scenes.text: The first model is local: it cuts false accepts by seventy-five percent, but blocks half of the correct citations. Out. The decision model over the A P I scores thirty out of thirty: zero false accepts, zero false rejects, about two hundred milliseconds per pair. Precise enough to switch on by default.

scenes.title: Faithful at write time
scenes.text: With the judge on, the agent can no longer staple a real quote to a sentence it does not support. Numbers, dates, negations: if they change, the citation is contradicted and the answer never ships. That is faithfulness at write time, not a score computed afterwards.

scenes.title: Before, not after
scenes.text: Recent benchmarks, like LA Quer, measure after the fact: a user highlights a sentence and a model checks whether the sources support it. We check before, while the agent is writing. Same question, different moment. And the numbers are not comparable: provenance alone is not enough.

scenes.title: Two proofs, one citation
scenes.text: Two proofs. The quote exists. And the quote is about the sentence. Without the second, the first is decoration. Citations verified. Now also relevant.
